Quick technical summary from infra/on-call (TL;DR):
- Root cause: transient control-plane partition between two AZs in us-west-2 that affected our internal leader-election. The autoscaler leader lost heartbeat visibility to controller agents in AZ-b, causing the allocation controller to mark nodes NotReady and block new allocations. This was exacerbated by a bug that suppressed immediate leader re-election for ~35 minutes when partial quorums were detected.
- Customer impact: queued requests + 5xx errors returned by our fronting gateway while the pool partially misreported capacity. Approximately 40 minutes of degraded throughput for Starlight's Dedicated pool.

Actions already taken:
- Forced leader re-election and reconciliation at 06:10 UTC; allocation resumed immediately and requests drained by 06:20.
- Deployed a hotfix to the election timeout logic to reduce the re-election window from 45s to 10s in partial-quorum scenarios (canary pass at 06:55).
- Increased cross-AZ heartbeat frequency + added additional health-check probes to reduce false NotReady states.

Next steps (post-incident):
- Postmortem draft (internal) is in the drive link; will add timeline + RCA + remediation plan.
- Prod hardening: add an autoscaler safety valve to funnel new allocations to unaffected AZs when partial quorums are detected; evaluate warm-standby pre-allocation options for customers on reserved pools.

Credit recommendation: 10% of the monthly Dedicated fee for the single day window, or an equivalent one-month warm-standby discount if they prefer capacity-based protection. Laura/Naomi please advise.

I'll join the customer 17:00 PDT sync to walk timeline and technical fixes.

—Karthik
